title: A matmul from movement ops
starter:
# C (2x2) = A (2x3) @ B (3x2), all row-major
%Ab = buffer 6 dtype=f32 slot=0
%Bb = buffer 6 dtype=f32 slot=1
%Cb = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=2
%A  = load %Ab
%B  = load %Bb
# the syllabus form: it assumes slot 0 holds A transposed
%a3t = reshape %A shape=[3 2 1]
%ax = expand %a3t shape=[3 2 2]
%b3 = reshape %B shape=[3 1 2]
%bx = expand %b3 shape=[3 2 2]
%p  = mul %ax %bx
%c  = reduce %p op=add pop=1
%cf = reshape %c shape=[4]
%s  = store %Cb %cf
%C1 = after %Cb %s

hints: Start from the syllabus form, which assumes slot 0 holds A already transposed (K x M). Slot 0 here holds A as M x K.
Reshape A to `[2 3 1]`, then `permute order=[1 0 2]` to get `[3 2 1]`: k first, then m. B reshapes to `[3 1 2]`.
Expand both to `[3 2 2]`, multiply, and `reduce op=add pop=1` sums over k. Reshape the `[2 2]` result to `[4]` before the store.

answer.code:
# C (2x2) = A (2x3) @ B (3x2), all row-major
%Ab = buffer 6 dtype=f32 slot=0
%Bb = buffer 6 dtype=f32 slot=1
%Cb = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=2
%A  = load %Ab
%B  = load %Bb
%a3 = reshape %A shape=[2 3 1]
%aT = permute %a3 order=[1 0 2]
%ax = expand %aT shape=[3 2 2]
%b3 = reshape %B shape=[3 1 2]
%bx = expand %b3 shape=[3 2 2]
%p  = mul %ax %bx
%c  = reduce %p op=add pop=1
%cf = reshape %c shape=[4]
%s  = store %Cb %cf
%C1 = after %Cb %s
answer.explain: Putting k first lets `reduce pop=1` fold over it, in order k = 0, 1, 2, for every (m, n) at once. The permute is the transpose the syllabus form leaves to whoever fills the buffer.
